newsitem.title: UK: UK firms to rely on advisers for pensions - report.
newsitem.headline: UK firms to rely on advisers for pensions - report.

text.p: Independent financial advisers (IFAs) will hold on to their share of the increasingly complex corporate pensions and employee benefits market, said management consultancy Datamonitor.

"The rising costs of corporate protection, the introduction of the provisions of the Pensions Act and the increase in new products on offer will strengthen the channel's grip on the market," a Datamonitor report, UK Corporate Pensions and Employee Benefits 1996, said.
IFAs account for 78 percent of sales of corporate pension schemes run by insurance companies in the UK, Datamonitor said, adding that bancassurers will, however, become more competitive.
This will put particular pressure on life insurers' direct sales forces.

"Although little has altered in the distribution of corporate pensions and employee benefits, in the years to come there could be major changes with the entrance of bancassurers," the report said. "This means life offices will face even greater competition and will have to improve their service."
Datamonitor also expects "cafeteria benefits," where employees choose from a range of benefits offered by the employer, will be widely available in the UK within two years.
Prudential Corp Plc is market leader for group annual pensions with 22.4 percent of the market in 1995.

Datamonitor singled out Legal and General and Clerical Medical, which is merging with Halifax Building Society, with 3.6 percent and 10.4 percent of the market respectively, as performing well due to their reliance on IFAs.
